# Scalarization of Vector Fields

Also called: Vector Field Scalarization, Metric Scalarization

## Overview
Scalarization of Vector Fields converts multi-component vector data into a single scalar value per voxel, enabling the use of standard volume rendering or iso-surface extraction techniques that require scalar inputs [S1, unofficial]. It sets itself apart from direct vector visualization methods (like [Stream Lines](4796-stream-lines.md)) by collapsing directional information into intensity or opacity, and from tensor methods by focusing on derived scalar metrics (magnitude, divergence, helicity) rather than eigenstructure [S1, unofficial].

## Shared principles
All methods in this family evaluate a mapping function $M(\mathbf{x})$ at sample points $\mathbf{x}$ within the volume to produce visual attributes [G]. The core mechanism involves sampling the multi-component data field at $\mathbf{x}$, decomposing or normalizing the value (e.g., extracting magnitude, direction, eigenvalues, or phase), and applying a transfer function or geometric construction to map these features to rendering parameters such as color, opacity, or primitive geometry [G].

## Subtopics

### [Helicity Visualization](8393-helicity-visualization.md)
Helicity Visualization is a scalarization technique for vector fields that maps the dot product of velocity and vorticity to opacity and color to identify vortices. It sets itself apart from siblings like [Metric Scalar Field Rendering from Vector Fields](14065-metric-scalar-field-rendering-from-vector-fields.md) by explicitly leveraging the alignment between flow direction and local rotation (curl) to highlight swirling features, whereas metric methods often rely on magnitude or strain. See [Helicity Visualization](8393-helicity-visualization.md) for implementation details.

### [Metric Scalar Field Rendering from Vector Fields](14065-metric-scalar-field-rendering-from-vector-fields.md)
Metric Scalar Field Rendering converts vector field data into scalar values to enable standard surface or volume rendering techniques. It solves the problem of visualizing vector fields, which lack a single intensity value, by calculating metrics such as velocity magnitude, vorticity, or divergence. It differs from [Helicity Visualization](8393-helicity-visualization.md) by focusing on general magnitude-based scalarization rather than the specific alignment of curl and velocity. See [Metric Scalar Field Rendering from Vector Fields](14065-metric-scalar-field-rendering-from-vector-fields.md) for implementation details.

### Velocity Component Visualization
- **Definition**: Visualizing specific components of the velocity field (e.g., x-component) to identify flow separation and reversal [S1, unofficial].
- **Steps**: Map the smallest x velocity values (including negative values) to cyan and high opacity. Map the largest x velocity components to yellow and near transparency [S1, unofficial].

## Background
Originating in early computational fluid dynamics (CFD) visualization, this approach was detailed in "Volume Rendering for Computational Fluid Dynamics: Initial Results" (NASA, 1991) [S1, unofficial]. It addresses the limitation of early volume renderers which primarily supported scalar data, allowing researchers to visualize complex vector phenomena like vortices and flow separation by deriving meaningful scalar metrics [S1, unofficial].
